readings.title: Making the Ark
readings.subtitle: The Throne of Mercy Constructed
readings.text: [Exodus 37:1] And Betsal’ĕl made the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high. [2] And he overlaid it with clean gold inside and outside, and made a moulding of gold all around it. [3] And he cast four rings of gold for it, for its four feet, two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side. [4] And he made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold. [5] And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to lift the ark. [6] And he made the lid of atonement of clean gold, two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide. [7] And he made two keruḇim of beaten gold, he made them from the two ends of the lid of atonement, [8] one keruḇ at this end on this side, and the other keruḇ at that end on that side. He made the keruḇim from the lid of atonement, from the two ends. [9] And the keruḇim spread out their wings above, and covered the lid of atonement with their wings, with their faces toward each other, the faces of the keruḇim were turned toward the lid of atonement.

readings.title: Making the Table
readings.subtitle: For the Bread of Presence
readings.text: [Exodus 37:10] And he made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, and a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high. [11] And he overlaid it with clean gold, and made a moulding of gold all around it. [12] And he made a rim of a handbreadth all around it, and made a moulding of gold for the rim all around it. [13] And he cast four rings of gold for it, and put the rings on the four corners that were at its four legs. [14] The rings were close to the rim, as holders for the poles to lift the table. [15] And he made the poles of acacia wood to lift the table, and overlaid them with gold. [16] And he made the utensils which were on the table, its dishes, and its cups, and its bowls, and its jars for pouring, of clean gold.

readings.title: Making the Menorah
readings.subtitle: Beaten Work of Pure Gold
readings.text: [Exodus 37:17] And he made the lampstand of clean gold. He made the lampstand of beaten work, its base, and its shaft, its cups, its ornamental knobs, and its flowers were from it. [18] And six branches came out of its sides: three branches of the lampstand out of one side, and three branches of the lampstand out of the other side. [19] Three cups made like almond flowers on one branch, with an ornamental knob and a flower, and three cups made like almond flowers on the other branch, with an ornamental knob and a flower – so for the six branches coming out of the lampstand. [20] And on the lampstand were four cups made like almond flowers, its ornamental knobs and its flowers. [21] And a knob was under the first two branches of the same, and a knob under the second two branches of the same, and a knob under the third two branches of the same, for the six branches coming out of it. [22] Their knobs and their branches were from it, all of it was one beaten work of clean gold. [23] And he made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its trays, of clean gold. [24] He made it of a talent of clean gold, and all its utensils.

readings.title: Making the Altar of Incense
readings.subtitle: The Anointing Oil and Incense
readings.text: [Exodus 37:25] And he made the incense altar of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide – square – and two cubits high. Its horns were of the same. [26] And he overlaid it with clean gold, its top and its sides all around, and its horns. And he made a moulding for it of gold all around. [27] And he made two rings of gold for it under its moulding, by its two corners on both sides, as holders for the poles with which to lift it. [28] And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold. [29] And he made the set-apart anointing oil, and the clean sweet incense, the work of a perfumer.

readings.title: Making the Altar of Burnt Offering
readings.subtitle: Bronze and Acacia
readings.text: [Exodus 38:1] And he made the altar of ascending offering of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide – square – and three cubits high. [2] And he made its horns on its four corners, the horns were of the same. And he overlaid it with bronze. [3] And he made all the utensils for the altar: the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, and the forks, and the fire holders. He made all its utensils of bronze. [4] And he made a grating of bronze network for the altar, under its rim, midway from the bottom. [5] And he cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles. [6] And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with bronze. [7] And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, with which to lift it. He made the altar hollow with boards.

readings.title: The Bronze Basin
readings.subtitle: Made from the Mirrors of the Women
readings.text: [Exodus 38:8] And he made the basin of bronze and its base of bronze, from the bronze mirrors of the serving women who did service at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

readings.title: Making the Courtyard
readings.subtitle: Hangings, Pillars, and Sockets
readings.text: [Exodus 38:9] And he made the courtyard: for the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of fine woven linen, one hundred cubits, [10] their twenty columns and their twenty sockets, of bronze. The hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver. [11] And for the north side one hundred cubits, their twenty columns and their twenty sockets, of bronze. The hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver. [12] And for the west side hangings of fifty cubits, their ten columns and their ten sockets. The hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver. [13] And for the east side eastward fifty cubits: [14] fifteen cubits of hangings on the one side, with their three columns and their three sockets, [15] and fifteen cubits of hangings on the other side of the courtyard gate, on this side and on that side, with their three columns and their three sockets. [16] All the hangings of the courtyard all around were of fine woven linen. [17] And the sockets for the columns were of bronze, the hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver, and the overlay of their tops was of silver, and all the columns of the courtyard had bands of silver. [18] And the screen for the gate of the courtyard was the work of a weaver, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen, and twenty cubits long, and the height along the width was five cubits, corresponding to the hangings of the courtyard. [19] And there were four columns, and their four sockets of bronze, their hooks of silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands was of silver. [20] And all the pegs of the Dwelling Place, and of the courtyard all around, were of bronze.

readings.title: Inventory of Materials
readings.subtitle: Gold, Silver, and Bronze
readings.text: [Exodus 38:21] These were the appointments of the Dwelling Place, the Dwelling Place of the Witness, which was appointed by the mouth of Mosheh, for the service of the Lewites, by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aharon the priest. [22] And Betsal’ĕl son of Uri, son of Ḥur, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, made all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [23] And with him was Oholiaḇ son of Aḥisamaḵ, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and designer, a weaver in blue and purple and scarlet material, and in fine linen. [24] All the gold prepared for the work, in all the work of the Set-apart Place, was the gold of the wave offering, twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty sheqels, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place. [25] And the silver from those who were counted of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five sheqels, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place: [26] a beqa for a head, half a sheqel, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place, for everyone passing over to those who were counted, from twenty years old and above, for six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men. [27] And from the hundred talents of silver were cast the sockets of the Set-apart Place and the sockets of the veil: one hundred sockets from the hundred talents, a talent for a socket. [28] And of the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five sheqels he made hooks for the columns, and overlaid their tops, and made bands for them. [29] And the bronze of the wave offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred sheqels. [30] And with it he made the sockets for the door of the Tent of Meeting, and the bronze altar, and the bronze grating for it, and all the utensils of the altar, [31] and the sockets of the courtyard all around, and the sockets of the courtyard gate, and all the pegs of the Dwelling Place, and all the pegs of the courtyard all around.

readings.title: Garments for Service
readings.subtitle: As YeHoVaH Commanded Mosheh
readings.text: [Exodus 39:1] And of the blue and purple and scarlet material they made woven garments to do service in the Set-apart Place, and they made the set-apart garments which were for Aharon, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: Making the Shoulder Garment
readings.subtitle: Gold, Blue, Purple, and Scarlet
readings.text: [Exodus 39:2] And he made the shoulder garment of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen. [3] And they beat the gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads, to work it in with the blue and purple and scarlet material, and the fine linen, the work of a skilled workman. [4] They made shoulder pieces for it to be joined, it was joined at its two edges. [5] And the embroidered band of his shoulder garment that was on it was of the same work, of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [6] And they worked the shoham stones, set in enclosures of gold, engraved, as signets are engraved, with the names of the sons of Yisra’ĕl. [7] And he put them on the shoulder pieces of the shoulder garment, stones of remembrance for the sons of Yisra’ĕl, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: Making the Breastplate
readings.subtitle: Twelve Stones of Remembrance
readings.text: [Exodus 39:8] And he made the breastplate, the work of a skilled workman, like the work of the shoulder garment, of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen. [9] It was square, they made the breastplate double, a span its length and a span its width, double. [10] And they filled it with four rows of stones, a row of ruby, a topaz, and an emerald was the first row; [11] and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond; [12] and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; [13] and the fourth row a beryl, a shoham, and a jasper – set in enclosures of gold in their settings. [14] And the stones were according to the names of the sons of Yisra’ĕl, twelve according to their names, engraved like a signet, each one with its own name, for the twelve tribes. [15] And they made braided chains of corded work for the breastplate at the ends, of clean gold. [16] And they made two enclosures of gold and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate. [17] And they put the two cords of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate. [18] And the two ends of the two cords they fastened in the two enclosures, and put them on the shoulder pieces of the shoulder garment, at the front. [19] And they made two gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the edge of it, which was on the inward side of the shoulder garment. [20] And they made two gold rings, and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the shoulder garment, underneath and on the front, at its seam above the embroidered band of the shoulder garment. [21] And they bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the shoulder garment with a blue cord, to be above the embroidered band of the shoulder garment, and that the breastplate did not come loose from the shoulder garment, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Robe and Other Garments
readings.subtitle: Pomegranates and Bells
readings.text: [Exodus 39:22] And he made the robe of the shoulder garment of woven work, all of blue. [23] And the opening of the robe was in the middle, like the opening of a coat of mail, with a woven binding all around the opening, so that it would not tear. [24] And they made on the hem of the robe pomegranates of blue and purple and scarlet material, twined. [25] And they made bells of clean gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around between the pomegranates: [26] a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe to do service, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [27] And they made the long shirts of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aharon and his sons, [28] and the turban of fine linen, and the head-dresses of esteem of fine linen, and the linen trousers of fine woven linen, [29] and the girdle of fine woven linen with blue and purple and scarlet material, the work of an embroiderer, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [30] And they made the plate of the set-apart sign of dedication of clean gold, and wrote on it an inscription like the engraving of a signet: SET-APART TO <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [31] And they put on it a blue cord, to fasten it above on the turban, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.
